summary: - _b) Direct Respondent No. 3 to process and give effect to the Petitioner’s Standing Clearance request for the month of May 2026 without insisting on DISCOM consent as pre-condition;_ - _e) Pass such other order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit in the facts and circumstances of the present case.”_ - _b) Pass any other order or direction as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit in light of facts and circumstances of the present Petition._ - _b) An ex-parte ad interim direction to the Respondents to process, allow and give effect to the Standing Clearance dated 10.04.2026 already granted by Respondent No. 4 for the month of May 2026 without insisting on consent from Respondent No. 1 as a per-condition, pending disposal of the captioned Petition._ - (r) Accordingly, the Petitioner is constrained to approach this Commission by way of the present Petition, impugning the arbitrary conduct of Respondent No. 1 in imposing extraneous conditions and the threat of withholding of consent for subsequent months and the imposition of a non-statutory requirement of the DISCOM’s consent, as a mandatory requirement, by Respondent No. 3 in the grant of the Standing Clearance to the Petitioner. _2. After hearing the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission directed as under:_ _(c) The Respondents to file their replies to the Petition, if any, within two weeks with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its rejoinder, within two weeks thereafter.”_ - **(d)** Pursuant to letters dated 02.02.2026 and 30.03.2026, on 10.04.2026, the Petitioner sought clarification on issues arising from the demands raised by Respondent No. 1. The CEA clarified that: _“At the outset, learned senior counsel for the Respondent, TPCODL, submitted that the Petitioner, JSL, has not mapped the ID of TPCODL on the e-filing portal; therefore, TPCODL was unable to access the main Petition and the accompanying IAs. Accordingly, he prayed for additional time to file the reply on maintainability and merits in respect of the Petition and IA No. 67/2026._ - **(l)** Petitioner failed to disclose material facts having direct bearing on the subject matter of the dispute, particularly the fact that consent/NOC had been sought under the OA Regulations, and therefore the conduct of the Petitioner deserves to be viewed seriously, and the Petition is liable to be dismissed on grounds of suppression of material facts and abuse of process of law. _“At the outset, the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner, JSL, submitted that vide the Record of Proceedings dated 6.5.2026, the Respondent, TPCODL, was permitted to file its reply to the IA as well as the Petition on both counts, maintainability as well as merits. However, TPCODL has filed only a reply on the maintainability of the present Petition and not on the merits. He further submitted that, as regards the jurisdiction, the grievance in this case arises out of the issuance of standing clearance under the GNA Regulations, and the Commission has dealt with similar issues in the past, and one of such orders has also been upheld by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in a recent judgment. He also sought liberty to file/rely upon his note of arguments in this regard._ _2. Learned senior counsel for the Respondent, TPCODL, while relying on the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Ramayana Ispat (P) Ltd. v. State of Rajasthan, [(2025) 8 SCC 747], submitted that the Commission lacks jurisdiction to adjudicate the present dispute and thus the present Petition ought to be rejected. He also requested that the Petitioner’s note of arguments may be shared with TPCODL._ _4. Considering the above, the Commission permitted the Respondents, OPTCL and Odisha SLDC, to file their respective replies in the matter, if not already done so, within a week. The Petitioner was also permitted to file a brief note in the matter within two days, with a copy to the Respondents._ - **(c)** Somehow to overcome the issue of maintainability, the Petitioner has placed reliance on the response of the CEA dated 10.04.2026. In this regard, it is submitted that, to begin with, the said response is based solely on the Petitioner’s case, without any opportunity being accorded to OPTCL to state its position. In any event, the CEA acts in an advisory capacity, and its views cannot be treated as the last word. It is submitted that treating the response of the CEA as binding would run counter to the scheme of the Electricity Act. **3.** During the hearing, parties argued at length on the aspects of the jurisdiction and interim relief(s) for the month of June 2026. Learned Senior Counsel for Petitioner submitted that it is settled law that an interim relief is granted in aid of, and ancillary to the main relief, and therefore, the Commission ought to consider such relief(s) for June 2026 as well. Considering the request of the learned senior counsel and learned counsel for the parties, the Commission permitted both sides to file their respective note by tomorrow, and the matter was reserved for Order. **12.** I We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and Respondents and perused the documents available on record. It is well-settled that the issue of maintainability, going to the jurisdiction of this Commission, must be decided as a threshold question before embarking on the merits of the dispute . The first and foremost issue that arises for our consideration is ‘ **Whether this Commission has jurisdiction to adjudicate the dispute in the instant Petition related to non-grant of Standing Clearance by the Odisha SLDC for an intra-State entity, for transactions under T-GNA?** **22.** Based on the foregoing, we are of the view that the matter under the present Petition is beyond the jurisdictional power of this Commission. Accordingly, the Petition as well as the related Interlocutory Application are rejected. The Petitioner may approach the Appropriate Commission for adjudication of the issues under the instant Petition.
